chapter_title: Chương 74: Tôi Đến Để Dạy Các Bạn Một Bài Học

segments.title: Chương 74: Tôi Đến Để Dạy Các Bạn Một Bài Học
segments.content:
"Li Jun, aren't you going to the multimedia classroom?"

"What's the point of listening to Chen Guiliang's lecture! Come on, let's go play basketball."

"That's not very nice. We're all classmates, we should at least show some support."

"Whatever. Basketball, basketball, anyone who wants to play basketball, come on."

"..."

Li Jun hugged his basketball and shouted repeatedly. Sure enough, four or five boys decided not to attend Chen Guiliang's "lecture" and joined Li Jun to play basketball instead.

To support Chen Guiliang, the head teacher had moved PE class to this time.

The students of Class 11, Year 3 could choose to have free time or to support Chen Guiliang.

As for students from other classes, regardless of their year, as long as they weren't in a regular class, they could go and join in the excitement.

Bian Guanyue and Wu Meng walked side by side, discussing in low voices.

"Do you know what he's going to talk about?" Wu Meng asked.

Bian Guanyue shook her head. "No idea."

"He borrowed your laptop to make his presentation. How could you not know?"

"I really don't. He's been so mysterious these past few days."

"I'm actually quite looking forward to it. I'm sure he'll have something new to say."

"..."

The multimedia classroom was in the Laboratory Building which, like the Library Building, was built during Principal Yan's tenure.

The Laboratory Building, of course, had physics and chemistry labs. There were also computer rooms and a multimedia classroom specifically for lectures and large classes.

The first and second-year students always had computer classes.

That time Chen Guiliang started a petition demanding a refund for the computer fee was purely because the third-year curriculum was tight, so the year-level coordinators canceled computer classes, but the school forgot to refund the fee.

It might have been poor communication between the year-level coordinators and the finance office, or perhaps the finance office pretended not to know.

More likely, everyone knew, but thought it was better to let sleeping dogs lie!

Because refunding the money required getting a leader's signature and the process was rather troublesome, with the potential of offending a leader, the finance office simply chose to stay silent.

That money was probably sitting in the school's account. The week after Chen Guiliang started the joint petition, the school promptly refunded the money to the third-year students.

As the students of Class 11, Year 3 headed to the multimedia classroom, the school leaders were also accompanying media reporters there.

There were also some Chinese language teachers.

When they arrived at the entrance of the multimedia classroom, they saw Chen Guiliang on the stage, adjusting the equipment.

A reporter immediately took out his camera and snapped a few photos of Chen Guiliang.

Among the school leaders, Zhong Dahe, a geography teacher and vice principal, was the most familiar with Chen Guiliang. He walked over and asked, "Can you handle this yourself?"

"No problem."

Chen Guiliang replied with a smile, then tested the microphone, "Hello, hello, hello~~~"

The reporters, who had come from big cities, had been jolted on the broken roads yesterday and had low expectations for this small county's school. Now, walking into the multimedia classroom and seeing a student adjusting the equipment, they felt that No. 2 Middle School's hardware was actually not bad.

Principal Yan was very pleased at this moment. His main goal was to showcase the school's software and hardware.

Especially the high-tech hardware, all of which was his handiwork!

He had also arranged other activities for the afternoon, such as having some students go to the electronic reading room, and then inviting media reporters to visit and take pictures.

The seats for leaders and reporters quickly filled up.

Before long, the students from Class 11 also arrived, all taking their seats in the student and teacher section. Some teachers and students from other classes also trickled in to see what was going on.

Chen Guiliang looked at the clock on the wall and, after a brief wait, finally began to speak. "Esteemed reporters, leaders, teachers, and fellow students, I'm very happy to meet with you all today to discuss some key points of high school Chinese. I am just an ordinary student, not qualified to teach you, but I would like to offer a few personal views. To cast a brick to attract a jade, for your reference only..."

As he spoke, Chen Guiliang clicked the mouse, and the full text of the "Preface to the Pavilion of Prince Teng" was projected onto the screen.

"The 'Preface to the Pavilion of Prince Teng' is a masterpiece for the ages, and I'm sure everyone is very familiar with it. But when I was studying it, I also had some questions..."

"First, we should understand the genre of this piece. What is a preface? Can anyone here answer that?"

Xu Haibo was very supportive and immediately raised his hand.

Chen Guiliang smiled. "Please, this student."

Xu Haibo stood up and said, "A preface is a foreword or introduction. It can be a preface to an article, a poem, or a book."

"What about the 'Preface to the Orchid Pavilion Collection' then?" Chen Guiliang guided.

Xu Haibo added, "It can also be a preface for an event."

"Thank you, please be seated."

Chen Guiliang clicked the mouse again, and the definition of "preface" appeared on the projector screen.

"The first type of preface is an introduction to a book or article. The second type is a descriptive text for an event. So, which category does the 'Preface to the Pavilion of Prince Teng' belong to?"

Chen Guiliang looked towards the reporters' section. "Would any reporter friend like to answer?"

A reporter from the Rongcheng Business Daily played along, "It's a bit of both. It's a preface for the banquet, and also a preface for his own poem."

Chen Guiliang shook his head. "It's almost impossible for it to be both."

The reporter was taken aback, and other reporters let out soft laughs.

"'Each man is given a topic, and four rhymes are all composed.' The textbook's annotation is: 'My poem is laid out, forming four rhymes.' This indicates that he is writing a preface for his own poem."

"Was Wang Bo really writing a preface for his own poem? Has anyone heard any interesting stories about this banquet?"

Chen Guiliang looked out at the audience.

Class president Li Rui raised his hand. "Our Chinese teacher told us in class. The host of the banquet was the local governor, who wanted to show off his son-in-law. So, no one else dared to write, or they deliberately wrote poorly. But Wang Bo didn't understand the ways of the world, and his 'Preface to the Pavilion of Prince Teng' stunned everyone. Because it was so well-written, the governor wasn't angry and even praised Wang Bo as a genius. Wang Bo had no official rank at the time, and no one thought much of him before he wrote the piece. After writing it, he became famous."

This story is widely known because it has the satisfying trope of a dark horse's triumphant comeback.

Not only had the students heard it, but most of the reporters present had also heard it.

Chen Guiliang clicked the mouse and pointed to the projection screen, saying, "I couldn't find where this story first originated. But there is a record in the 'New Book of Tang: Biography of Wang Bo,' which says that no one else dared to write, and only Wang Bo dared to pick up the brush. The Governor of Hongzhou was so angry he went to the lavatory. Every time Wang Bo wrote a few lines, an official would go to the lavatory to report. Before he had even finished hearing the entire piece, the governor was already calling him a genius."

"It also says that Wang Bo didn't even need to think carefully. He would get drunk and sleep, and when he woke up, he would write, producing a complete work without changing a single word. The term 'fù gǎo' (mental draft) comes from this anecdote."

"I thank the school for opening the library, allowing me to look up the 'New Book of Tang'."

Principal Yan was extremely pleased to hear this last sentence; he too had a hand in cultivating a literary genius.

The media reporters and the school's teachers and students also listened with great interest, and even learned the origin of the term "fù gǎo."

"The 'New Book of Tang' is just pure fabrication!"

Chen Guiliang suddenly dropped a bombshell, his voice resolute.

The audience below immediately perked up.

A high school student daring to declare that the 'New Book of Tang' was fabricated?

Chen Guiliang clicked the mouse again. "The civil service examinations and officialdom of the Tang Dynasty were different from those of the Song, Ming, and Qing dynasties. Although the Tang Dynasty also had civil service exams, becoming an official was mainly based on recommendations. Family background was more important than examination results."

"And Wang Bo came from the Wang clan of Hedong, a branch of the Wang clan of Taiyuan. There's a line in the 'Three Character Classic': 'The Five Masters include Xun and Yang, Wen Zhongzi, as well as Lao and Zhuang.' This 'Wen Zhongzi' was Wang Tong, who was none other than Wang Bo's grandfather!"

"When the people of the Song Dynasty compiled the 'Three Character Classic', they listed Wang Bo's grandfather alongside Laozi, Zhuangzi, Xunzi, and Yang Xiong as the Five Masters. One can imagine how prominent Wang Bo's background was. In the Tang Dynasty, which placed great emphasis on lineage, would a local governor dare to give Wang Bo a hard time?"

"When Ouyang Xiu compiled the 'New Book of Tang', he projected the official environment of the Song Dynasty onto it, without carefully examining the situation in the Tang Dynasty. At least in the section on Wang Bo's biography, the 'New Book of Tang' is definitely a fabrication!"

A reporter from the Shancheng Evening News raised his hand and said, "The 'Three Character Classic' was written in the Southern Song Dynasty. Perhaps Wang Tong wasn't famous in the Tang Dynasty, and his status only rose in the Song Dynasty."

"That's also a possibility."

Chen Guiliang smiled and clicked the mouse. A string of article titles appeared on the screen.

Chen Guiliang said, "'The Collected Works of Wang Zian' is very difficult to buy. It's not available in Xinhua Bookstore, nor can it be found online. Last week, I asked Principal Yan to take me to the library of the Sichuan University of Science and Engineering in our city, and I was fortunate enough to find a 1995 edition of the 'Annotated Collected Works of Wang Zian'."

"In this collection of Wang Bo's works, there are more than forty prefaces. Over half of them, just like the 'Preface to the Pavilion of Prince Teng', were prefaces written by Wang Bo at banquets. This means that wherever Wang Bo went, he was a star. He was the one to write the prefaces for banquets."

"And Wang Bo died just two years after writing the 'Preface to the Pavilion of Prince Teng'. Most of these other prefaces were written even earlier. Wang Bo was already famous long before. Would the Governor of Hongzhou dare to bully him? This also serves as evidence that the 'New Book of Tang' is a fabrication."

The teachers and reporters in the audience were already convinced by Chen Guiliang.

Because on the projection screen, there was a dense list of Wang Bo's "Preface to XXX." The titles of those prefaces were either related to banquets or to travel, all involving gatherings of officials and scholars.

The story of Wang Bo being bullied by the Governor of Hongzhou and discriminated against by the scholars present was definitely false.

The related content in the 'New Book of Tang' was also false.

At every banquet, Wang Bo was the brightest star of the show!

Chen Guiliang continued clicking the mouse. "Many of Wang Bo's prefaces contain phrases like 'yī yán jūn fù' (each man is given a topic), or 'rén cǎi yī zì' (each man picks a character), 'rén fēn yī zì' (each man is assigned a character), 'rén fù yī yán' (each man is given a topic). These are closely followed by words like 'sì yùn' (four rhymes) or 'liù yùn' (six rhymes)."

"If we follow the annotation in the Chinese textbook, it means he has finished writing his own poem. Is it necessary to mention such nonsense every time?"

"Let's now look at the banquet prefaces of other Tang Dynasty poets."

The reporters, leaders, teachers, and students looked at the projection screen, which showed excerpts from several prefaces by the Four Paragons of the Early Tang.

All of them contained phrases similar to "each man is given a topic, and four rhymes are all composed."

Clearly, this wasn't some polite formula, but a standard format for banquet prefaces.

Chen Guiliang continued, "When scholars of the Sui and Tang dynasties gathered to write poetry, they also had to follow rules. The host of the banquet would select many characters as rhyming words in advance. Participants would be assigned a character on the spot, and the poems they wrote had to rhyme with that character. The number of lines to be written would also be specified."

"'Yī yán jūn fù' means each person chooses a character for rhyming, and everyone writes a poem together."

"'Sì yùn jù chéng' means everyone's poem must have four rhymes, and must be eight lines long."

"These two lines are Wang Bo announcing the rules for writing poetry. It's not like the textbook annotation says, that I have finished writing my own poem!"

The people present, including the students, had a sudden realization upon hearing this.

Principal Yan even started clapping on the spot, leading everyone to applaud together.

After the applause ended, Chen Guiliang continued:

"When writing poems at a banquet, the title also has a fixed format. It must specify which character was assigned to you as the rhyme. This makes it easier for everyone to judge the quality and determine if there were any rule violations."

"For example, Wang Bo's 'Shangsi Fu Jiang Yan Yun De Zhi Zi' (At the Shangsi Festival Floating on the River Banquet, Obtaining the Rhyme Character 'Zhi'), and Song Zhiwen's 'Pei Qun Gong Deng Ji Shan Fu De Qun Zi' (Accompanying the Gentlemen Ascending Mount Ji and Obtaining the Rhyme Character 'Qun')."

"Therefore, the 'Poem on the Pavilion of Prince Teng' in our Chinese textbook is also a forgery!"

Chen Guiliang threw out another bombshell.

Many reporters had already sat up straight. They had a story to write now.

"Why is the 'Poem on the Pavilion of Prince Teng' a forgery? First, its title doesn't conform to the format."

"Second, the 'Poem on the Pavilion of Prince Teng' has six rhymes, which doesn't conform to the 'sì yùn jù chéng' (four rhymes are all composed) rule given in the 'Preface'. The poem also changes its rhyme scheme midway, which doesn't conform to the 'yī yán jūn fù' (each man is given a topic) rule given in the 'Preface'."

Fearing that those present might not understand, Chen Guiliang had also circled and marked the six rhymes of the 'Poem on the Pavilion of Prince Teng' when he was making his PPT.

Then, Chen Guiliang concluded:

"The full title of the 'Preface to the Pavilion of Prince Teng' is 'Autumn Day Ascending the Pavilion of Prince Teng in Hongzhou for a Farewell Banquet, a Preface'. This indicates that Wang Bo was attending a farewell banquet."

"The correct translation of the last paragraph is: I am honored to be invited to this farewell banquet, and I boldly record the grand occasion and leave some parting words. As for the task of writing poems, I leave it to all of you present. I have presumptuously written this preface, assigning each person a character for rhyming; everyone must compose a poem of four rhymes and eight lines. Please, all of you, display your talents to the fullest!"

"Therefore, it can be concluded that the 'Preface to the Pavilion of Prince Teng' was written after the banquet began but before the poetry writing started. It served as the opening remarks for the banquet's poetry session, where Wang Bo, on behalf of the Governor of Hongzhou, set the tone and announced the rules for the session."

Chen Guiliang let go of the mouse and said to the audience, "So, the textbook's annotation for 'yī yán jūn fù, sì yùn jù chéng' is absurdly wrong, leading students to misunderstand the entire article and its creative context. Moreover, the 'Poem on the Pavilion of Prince Teng' presented later in the textbook is also a forgery."

"I suggest that it be changed the next time the Chinese language textbook is compiled."

"Additionally, when compiling the textbook, many reference books were surely consulted. Those reference books are probably all wrong too."

"The annotation in the 2002 'Guwen Guanzhi' published by Jiangsu Province Ancient Books Publishing House that I bought is correct, but the one in the 1988 'Guwen Guanzhi' from Yuelu Publishing House that my Chinese teacher bought is wrong. However, both editions of 'Guwen Guanzhi' included the forged poem."

"I suggest that the relevant reference books be revised as well!"

The media reporters on site were already drafting headlines in their minds.

Literary Prodigy Questions Chinese Textbook, Suggests Education Department Revise Teaching Materials.

High School Student Cites Classics to Refute Errors in 'New Book of Tang' and Chinese Textbook.

Genius Teen's Profound Knowledge of Classical Chinese, Why Shouldn't Prestigious Universities Make an Exception for Admission?

A Discussion on the Flaws in Contemporary Chinese Language Education: Why is the Textbook Compilation Committee of Experts Outmatched by a Third-Year High School Student?
